channel.title: Israel National News Flashes
channel.description: Latest news flashes from Israel National News

item.title: Rabbi Kenneth Brander: ‘There is nothing Jewish about terrorizing innocent people'
item.description: Ohr Torah Stone President Rabbi Dr. Kenneth Brander condemns the attack on Jalud, calling for those responsible to be investigated and held accountable.

item.title: Antisemitism or political sabotage? Past quotes stir controversy in France
item.description: Mediapart published conversations from 2013 in which antisemitic statements are attributed to the president of the right-wing party. Bardella denies the allegations and has filed a defamation lawsuit.

item.title: Innocent? Death row inmate released from prison after 41 years
item.description: A man who spent 41 years on death row in the US after being convicted of killing a woman has been released on bail after prosecutors said a new analysis of DNA evidence did not link him to the crime.

item.title: Morocco makes history: King appoints first female prime minister
item.description: King Mohammed VI has appointed Fatima Ezzahra El Mansouri as Morocco’s prime minister after her party won the largest number of seats in the parliamentary elections.

item.title: “False blood libels": Netanyahu launches legal battle against media
item.description: Prime Minister files NIS 2.6 million defamation lawsuit against media outlets and journalists over reports that he received warnings before October 7.

item.title: Ireland won a game of Football 3-0. It lost everything else
item.description: Ireland can keep the three points, it must also own the ugliness it brought into the “Beautiful Game."

item.title: Reporters came to cover an accident, witnessed another accident
item.description: A TVP Info crew covering a fatal accident in Poland captured another crash as a car hit a 14-year-old girl on a scooter. The reporter and cameraman rushed to help.

item.title: Islamic preacher in Melbourne calls for taking up arms against Jews and Christians
item.description: Melbourne Islamic preacher calls in a sermon to reject Jews and Christians as friends and take up arms against them, amid criticism over Australia's response to extremist incitement.

item.title: Frankly my dear, I don’t give a damn
item.description: Antisemitism is so hip, so cool. Don’t these people know that they have moved to the side of the devil? Opinion.

item.title: Dramatic rescue: Paramedic climbs 55 meters to rescue construction worker
item.description: A construction worker lost consciousness in a crane cab in Kiryat Bialik. An MDA paramedic climbed 55 meters to treat him and he was evacuated to Rambam in stable condition.

item.title: “Our enemies will try to attack us": Lapid demands clarification from Netanyahu on threat
item.description: Netanyahu said there are indications that Israel’s enemies will attempt to attack ahead of the elections. Lapid demanded an urgent briefing, and Netanyahu instructed his military secretary to update him.

item.title: Smotrich orders preparations for additional fuel subsidies amid energy crisis
item.description: The Finance Minister instructed professional officials to prepare for additional subsidies on gasoline prices, in an effort to mitigate the expected increase amid the global energy crisis.

item.title: Yair Golan demands: 'Disqualify Otzma Yehudit'
item.description: After their request was rejected by the Central Elections Committee, the Democrats party petitioned the Supreme Court, demanding that Otzma Yehudit be disqualified from running for the Knesset.

item.title: Defense Minister threatens Hamas leaders abroad
item.description: Minister Katz responded to the elimination of the commander of Hamas' Northern Gaza Brigade and made clear that the defense establishment will continue pursuing the terrorist organization's senior leaders.

item.title: KKL-JNF clarifies: No parties will be held at Nova site
item.description: Ahead of the anniversary of October 7, KKL-JNF clarified that visits to the Nova site in the Re’im Forest will be permitted solely for remembrance and commemoration.

item.title: Israel's loitering munition waits to strike, now with a NATO connection
item.description: Israeli defense company UVision is partnering with Estonia’s LendurAI to integrate advanced AI and autonomous capabilities into its loitering munitions for an undisclosed NATO member state.

item.title: UK targets IDF: Blocks over 80 export licences
item.description: Britain has suspended or refused more than 80 export licences for items potentially used by the IDF in Gaza, the Jewish Chronicle reports.

item.title: Netanyahu: There are signs our enemies will try to attack us ahead of elections
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu said today at the Tel Nof Air Force Base that there are signs Israel’s enemies may attempt to attack the country ahead of the elections.
Netanyahu issued a warning to Israel’s enemies, saying: "Don’t mess with us. Our long arm will reach you anywhere, at any time."

item.title: Did Netanyahu secretly meet a Libyan leader in Abu Dhabi?
item.description: An aircraft used by Saddam Haftar reportedly landed in Abu Dhabi shortly after Netanyahu, prompting an unconfirmed claim that the two met.

item.title: Give honor to the Torah
item.description: The mitzvah of Torah study is equal to all the other mitzvot. The reward for the mitzvah of Torah study is equal to the reward of all the mitzvot. Every person of Israel who engages in Torah sustains the world.

item.title: Israel's weapon against boycotts - a boycott of the PA
item.description: Dr. Dan Diker urges Israel to use economic pressure against the Palestinian Authority and launch a more aggressive international campaign to counter boycotts of Israeli products.

item.title: El Al flight from TLV to Miami turns back several hours after takeoff due to malfunction
item.description:
El Al flight LY017 from Tel Aviv to Miami turned back toward Tel Aviv several hours after takeoff due to an unexpected technical malfunction.
Read more.

item.title: Morocco: Israel embassy plans spark protests across 45 cities
item.description: Protesters gathered across Morocco after Rabat and Jerusalem agreed to open embassies and exchange ambassadors, with police detaining several in Tangier.

item.title: AG and State Attorney back disqualification of Arab candidate
item.description: The Attorney General and State Attorney have declared support for the petition to disqualify Sami Abu Shahhdah from the Knesset for supporting a fight against Israel.

item.title: Katz: Rioters undermine security efforts, the settlement enterprise, and the State of Israel
item.description: Defense Minister Israel Katz condemned the riots while visiting Judea and Samaria alongside the head of the IDF Central Command, saying that those involved "divert forces from their missions and seriously undermine security efforts, the settlement enterprise, and the State of Israel." Katz emphasized that the rioters do not represent the settler population and called for decisive action against them and for those responsible to be brought to justice.

item.title: Netanyahu condemns Binyamin riots: 'Prosecute the rioters to the fullest extent of the law'
item.description:
Prime Minister Benjamin Netanyahu condemned on Tuesday morning the violent riots that took place overnight in the Binyamin region and the attacks on security forces who arrived at the scene.
"The handful of rioters does not represent the law-abiding settler population in Judea and Samaria; it does a tremendous injustice and interferes with our forces in carrying out their mission," Netanyahu said.
Netanyahu expressed his support for the IDF soldiers and Border Police officers operating in the area and called on law enforcement authorities to take action against those involved.
"I fully support the IDF soldiers and Border Police officers who are working to thwart terrorism and maintain security, and I call on law enforcement authorities to prosecute the rioters to the fullest extent of the law," he stated.

item.title: Fuel prices to hit record high overnight
item.description: Regulated fuel prices will rise during the night between Wednesday and Thursday by 52 agorot per liter for 95-octane gasoline.

item.title: Watch: Thousands sing and dance in Hebron
item.description: Approximately 10,000 worshipers, led by Rabbi Shmuel Eliyahu, prayed, sang, and danced at the Cave of the Patriarchs in Hebron.

item.title: Believe in the justice of our cause
item.description: An extract from “Bechayil U’v Ruach," the last book that Rav Chaim Druckman approved for publication before he passed away, less than a year before the start of the war in Gaza.

item.title: Labour? Friends of Israel? Burnham’s cabinet to skip pro-Israel reception
item.description: No members of Andy Burnham’s cabinet are expected at the Labour Friends of Israel reception, days after Ed Miliband addressed a Palestinian event.
